title: How Long Can Pizza Sit Out?

seo.title: How Long Can Pizza Sit Out?
seo.meta_description: Pizza with cheese, meat, or other perishable toppings follows the general rule of about 2 hours at room temperature, or 1 hour above 90°F (32°C).
seo.search_intent: Make a safe decision about “how long can pizza sit out,” recognize signals that require stopping or escalating, and know when to discard, evacuate, or get help as appropriate.

excerpt: Pizza with cheese, meat, or other perishable toppings follows the general rule of about 2 hours at room temperature, or 1 hour above 90°F (32°C). Leaving it out overnight is not a safe exception.
content_html:
Pizza with cheese, meat, or other perishable toppings follows the general rule of about 2 hours at room temperature, or 1 hour above 90°F (32°C). Leaving it out overnight is not a safe exception.

Treat pizza as perishable food

Cheese, meats, and sauces can support microbial growth while warm. A dry crust does not make the assembled pizza shelf-stable.

Refrigerate leftovers promptly

Store slices in shallow containers or wrap them well so they cool quickly. You do not need to wait for them to become fully cool on the counter.

Overnight pizza should be discarded

Even if it looks and smells normal, it has spent too long in a temperature range that supports bacterial growth.

Reheating raises temperature but does not erase history

Reheat properly when appropriate, but do not use the oven or microwave to “rescue” pizza that sat out too long.
